function.uniprot_function: Tumor suppressor. Promotes rapid degradation of CTNNB1 and participates in Wnt signaling as a negative regulator. APC activity is correlated with its phosphorylation state. Activates the GEF activity of SPATA13 and ARHGEF4. Plays a role in hepatocyte growth factor (HGF)-induced cell migration. Required for MMP9 up-regulation via the JNK signaling pathway in colorectal tumor cells. Associates with both microtubules and actin filaments, components of the cytoskeleton. Plays a role in mediating the organization of F-actin into ordered bundles. Functions downstream of Rho GTPases and DIAPH1 to selectively stabilize microtubules. Acts as a mediator of ERBB2-dependent stabilization of microtubules at the cell cortex. Required for the localization of MACF1 to the cell membrane and this localization of MACF1 is critical for its function in microtubule stabilization.
function.molecular_function: Negative regulator of Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway; scaffold protein in destruction complex; microtubule-binding protein; actin cytoskeleton organizer
function.tissue_specificity: Widely expressed including brain, small intestine, colon, thymus, skeletal muscle, heart, prostate, lung, spleen, ovary, testis, kidney, placenta, and liver. Highly expressed in intestinal and colorectal epithelia where it plays critical roles in homeostasis of enterocyte renewal.

pathways.pathway_role_summary: APC is the central scaffold protein of the beta-catenin destruction complex, the master negative regulator of canonical Wnt signaling. In the absence of Wnt ligands, APC recruits beta-catenin via its 15aa and 20aa repeats, facilitates beta-catenin phosphorylation by GSK3B and CK1, and promotes beta-catenin ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. This prevents beta-catenin nuclear accumulation and TCF/LEF-mediated transcription. Wnt pathway activation disrupts the destruction complex. Mutations in APC (especially truncations in the mutation cluster region) are the initiating events in >80% of colorectal cancers, leading to constitutive Wnt signaling. APC also has Wnt-independent functions in microtubule stabilization, cell migration, chromosome segregation, and cytoskeletal organization.

disease_associations.description: Autosomal dominant pre-malignant disease characterized by hundreds to thousands of adenomatous polyps in the colon and rectum, usually progressing to malignancy. Caused by germline mutations in APC gene.
disease_associations.clinical_significance: Nearly 100% lifetime risk of colorectal cancer if untreated

disease_associations.description: Over 80% of sporadic colorectal cancers contain somatic mutations in APC, predominantly truncating mutations in the mutation cluster region (MCR) between codons 1286-1513. These mutations eliminate AXIN binding sites and most beta-catenin binding 20aa repeats.
disease_associations.clinical_significance: APC mutation is typically the initiating event in colorectal tumorigenesis via the adenoma-carcinoma sequence

metadata.data_quality_notes: High-quality data available for destruction complex interactions. Quantitative binding affinities well-characterized for APC-beta-catenin interaction (phosphorylated Kd ~10 nM, unphosphorylated Kd ~3 µM). APC-AXIN1 direct binding affinity less precisely measured experimentally (estimated ~100 nM from modeling). GSK3B-Axin binding well characterized (Kd 7.5-65 nM). APC contains extensive intrinsically disordered regions which complicate structural studies - only structured domains (N-terminus, armadillo repeats) have high-resolution structures. Most functional studies focus on truncated constructs. Disease mutations predominantly cluster in MCR (codons 1286-1513). Limited quantitative kinetic data for complex assembly/disassembly dynamics.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: APC is essential for quantitative modeling of Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway. Key parameters: (1) Beta-catenin binding affinity switches ~300-fold upon phosphorylation (3 µM → 10 nM), (2) Contains multiple binding sites (three 15aa repeats, seven 20aa repeats, three SAMP motifs) enabling multivalent interactions and cooperative assembly, (3) Scaffold function critical for destruction complex spatial organization and catalytic efficiency, (4) Truncation mutations (common in >80% CRC) eliminate specific binding sites - models must account for position-dependent effects, (5) APC concentration and stoichiometry vs Axin affects pathway sensitivity, (6) Phosphorylation-dependent binding provides switch-like behavior and feedback regulation. For destruction complex modeling: include multiple beta-catenin binding sites with different affinities, AXIN binding via SAMP repeats, and phosphorylation-dependent affinity changes.
